title: Period of small radial oscillations of a nudged circular orbit under an inverse-square force
summary: A particle on a circular orbit under F = -k/r^2 is nudged outward with its angular momentum unchanged and its distance oscillates. U_eff'' = k/r0^3 with r0 = l^2/(mk) gives T = 2 pi l^3/(mk^2) - option A - the same as the orbital period, so the orbit closes.
subject: Physics
topic: Radial oscillation of a nudged circular orbit under an inverse-square force - effective potential and a closed orbit
subtopics: Central force motion with conserved angular momentum
Effective potential U_eff = l^2/(2mr^2) - k/r and the circular orbit at its minimum
Inverse-square force: radial and orbital periods equal, closed (elliptical) orbits
concepts: With l fixed the radial motion is that of a particle in U_eff = l^2/(2mr^2) - k/r; the circular orbit is its minimum, r0 = l^2/(mk)
T = 2 pi sqrt(m r0^3/k) = 2 pi l^3/(m k^2) - option A - equal to the orbital period, so the nudged orbit closes (an ellipse)
Option B 2 pi sqrt(m/k) has the wrong units for k in N m^2 (the spring formula); C and D are a third and a fifth of the right value
For other power laws k/r^n the radial period is T_orbit/sqrt(3 - n) and the orbit traces a rosette
formulas: T = 2 pi sqrt(m r0^3/k) = 2 pi l^3/(m k^2)

methods: MathonGo solution (their Q22 = Physics Q.4) read first as the conceptual reference; its answer (A) agrees
Independent solve: U_eff''(r0) = k/r0^3 with r0 = l^2/(mk), omega^2 = k/(m r0^3), T = 2 pi l^3/(m k^2)
sympy: the minimum of U_eff, its second derivative, T = 2 pi/sqrt(U''/m) = 2 pi l^3/(mk^2) and the equal orbital period
scipy DOP853 integration (1e-12) of the radial equation: the period tends to the formula as dr -> 0 with an excess scaling as dr^2
Kepler: the integrated period equals 2 pi sqrt(m a^3/k) with a = r0 (1 + e)^2/(1 + 2e) at every nudge (1e-8)
Options audited: units of B; C and D a third and a fifth; for k/r^1.5 the radial period is T_orbit/sqrt(3 - n)
The page engine extracted and run in Node: answer A, its period equal to the DOP853 value (1e-5), l conserved, the orbit closing (apsis 360 deg), (A) across the slider range
